topic: BugbountyRules: Behavioral Discipline Skills That Turn an AI Agent Methodical

key_points: Primary source: 42 always-on behavioral rules (~1,489-line SKILL.md) governing how an agent hunts - scope, coverage, evidence, persistence - rather than shipping payloads

Bundled arsenal: portswigger-kb with 32 vulnerability-class folders / 93 sub-folders (~271 files), plus reference/ (8 files), writeup-library.md, waf-bypass-arsenal.md, vuln-taxonomy.md, vulnerability-rating-taxonomy.json, scripts/
Progressive disclosure: only SKILL.md is always in context; deep technique loads on demand so the agent is governed without carrying a library

Three named failure modes it targets: false positives (Hunter -> Skeptic -> Referee gate), severity inflation (per-metric anchoring, hedging language banned), quitting early (coverage ledger + depth ladders + stuck loop)
Two runtime mechanisms: the Hunt Reflex (pre-move checklist) and the Operational Flow (load prior state -> probe tool pack -> read scope -> passive recon -> map surface -> hunt -> verify -> report)
Rule 0 (Adaptive Thinking) is explicitly anti-robotic: tools are examples, not mandates; every target is different; includes an anti-pattern list of robotic behaviour
Multi-engine: Rule 3.12 offloads bulk reading to a local LLM (context firewall), Rule 3.14 sends findings and 'secure' conclusions to a frontier peer agent for a kill-gate / resurrection-gate

Evidence of measurement culture: the README states a small model put to eight findings waved through 3 of 4 textbook false positives and inflated severity on 6 of 8, and that ~1 in 5 real actions were exact duplicates
Repo facts (verified via GitHub API 2026-10-01): MIT, 35 stars / 6 forks, created 2026-08-17, last push 2026-08-18, no open issues, ~855 KB
Closest ecosystem competitor: a library of 93 single-SKILL.md offensive-security skills (bb-methodology, bb-recon, bb-verify, bb-report, hunt-* family) rather than one behavioural core
Verify-or-kill triage discipline: a 7-question gate on every finding before report-writing to keep the N/A ratio low
A->B->C chain-building economics: hunt-* skills ship as primitives with explicit 'chain to X' sections so CSRF becomes ATO and SSRF becomes cloud-metadata compromise
Per-class gate / verify / kill tables define what counts as proof (e.g. 'OOB callback or it didn't happen' for blind SSRF)
Modern classes covered: OWASP ASI01-ASI10 agentic AI security, CI/CD and GitHub Actions abuse, HTTP/2 single-packet races, protocol-version shadow APIs
Positioning contrast: breadth of classes vs bugbountyrules' depth of behaviour; methodology-as-library vs methodology-as-discipline
Repo facts (verified 2026-10-01): NOASSERTION license, 1 star, created 2026-08-28, last push 2026-09-26, ~831 KB
Trail of Bits bypassed ClawHub's malicious skill detector, Cisco's agent skill scanner, and all three scanners integrated into skills.sh
Three of four malicious skills were conceived and implemented in under an hour using standard tricks plus reading the scanner source

Bypasses: ~100,000 newlines to push payload past ClawHub's truncation window; malicious .pyc bytecode next to benign source; DOCX/ZIP archive indirection; and social-engineering the LLM-as-judge layer with compliance-policy-sounding prose
Conclusion is the ecosystem's key framing: 'no amount of scanning or LLM analysis can reliably detect malicious content in agent skills' - treat marketplaces as one layer, not a gate
Directly relevant because an always-loaded behavioural skill is exactly the class of artefact this research says scanners cannot validate
Hands-on comparison of 5 Claude Code security skills; the review rubric the article should meet or beat (read the SKILL.md, check the repo, look at what the skill actually instructs)

Winning skill (getsentry/skills@security-review) wins on the same axis bugbountyrules claims: it defines a methodology with a confidence system (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), false-positive awareness, data-flow tracing, and dozens of supporting reference files
Explicit takeaway: 'the difference between a thin checklist and a methodology is the difference between noise and signal'
Documents the install-count trap: an aggregator repo with 900+ skills inflated the top-ranked skill's installs, i.e. distribution metrics are not quality signals
OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (ASI01-ASI10), published 2025-12-09 by the GenAI Security Project's Agentic Security Initiative
ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities covers what agents load at runtime - MCP servers, plugins, prompt templates, tool descriptors, skills
ASI02 Tool Misuse, ASI03 Identity & Privilege Abuse, ASI06 Memory & Context Poisoning, ASI08 Cascading Failures, ASI10 Rogue Agents are the control categories a hunting skill's rules map onto
Two design principles: least agency (grant only the autonomy the task needs) and strong observability
Cited incidents for grounding: postmark-mcp first malicious MCP server in the wild (Koi Security, Sept 2025); EchoLeak CVE-2025-32711 (CVSS 9.3); Gemini memory-poisoning attack (Rehberger, Feb 2025)
A companion OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 (AST10) project formalises the skills behaviour layer as a first-class vulnerable component
Galileo research (Dec 2025): a single compromised agent poisoned 87% of downstream decisions within 4 hours in simulation
Quantifies the skill supply-chain problem: a large-scale study scanning 42,447 agent skills found 26.1% exhibit at least one security vulnerability
~5.2% of registry skills show signs of likely malicious intent; ClawHub hosted 49,592 community skills as of April 2026, implying 2,500+ potentially malicious packages
ClawHavoc campaign: 1,184 malicious skills introduced to ClawHub; five still evaded updated ClawScan and VirusTotal between Feb and May 2026

Structural limit worth citing in any skills article: formal static analysis (e.g. SkillFortify, 96.95% F1 on a 540-skill benchmark) cannot reason about natural-language instructions in SKILL.md because the consuming LLM interprets them at runtime
Recommendation: treat scanner passage as one signal among many, verify publisher identity out-of-band, and manually review SKILL.md behavioural directives

The bundled portswigger-kb knowledge base holds 32 vulnerability-class folders with 93 sub-folders (~271 files total in the repo), plus 8 reference files

angles: Discipline, not payloads: the core thesis that an agent already knows what SQLi is, so the failure is behavioural - and payloads cannot fix behaviour

The false-positive tax: a model waving through 3 of 4 planted false positives and inflating 6 of 8 severities is the reason triagers ignore agent reports; the Hunter -> Skeptic -> Referee gate is an adversarial self-review that mirrors OWASP ASI09/ASI10 controls

The coverage ledger as a duplicate killer: ~1 in 5 actions duplicated and ~20% of actions wasted by not reloading prior state after context compaction - the skill turns that measurement into Rule 21/28
Progressive disclosure as the context-budget answer: a 1,489-line behavioural core always loaded, a 32-class KB loaded on demand, so governance costs almost no tokens
Anti-robotic by design: Rule 0 exists because a rigid checklist is the failure mode, not the fix - contrast with static 'look for these patterns' security checklists

Scope enforcement is legal safety, not just tidiness: Rule 1 'one out-of-scope request can ban you from the programme', Rule 9 covers the two-way error (also refusing to write off in-scope assets for where they are hosted)

Honest-zero culture: Rule 25 refuses to conclude 'secure' while surface remains, but Rule 24 explicitly allows an honest zero over a fabricated finding - the opposite of the benchmark-gaming incentive around autonomous pentest agents

The ecosystem risk cut: a behavioural skill is an executable instruction bundle, so it inherits the skill supply-chain problem - OWASP ASI04, the Trail of Bits scanner bypass, and the 26,000-agent malicious skill are the context readers need before installing any third-party skill

One-core vs many-skills architecture: compare bugbountyrules' single always-on discipline against murrtada's 93 on-demand SKILL.md library and Sentry's confidence-tiered review skill - three different answers to the same trust problem

Measured over asserted: each rule carries the failure that justifies it, and run-eval.sh puts a rule's own text to an independent agent to prove it instructs rather than merely reads well - a verifiability claim worth testing in the article

The economics behind the demand for discipline: agents now reach HackerOne's top-3 on a $5,000/month budget while 58% of researchers say AI still misses business logic and chained exploits - discipline rules are the bridge those researchers are asking for
